title: fix(mcp): describe_object skips the hidden search companion on both transports
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D4Jsmd91BqTVB7dSii9uJMV)_
Fixes #33454
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

> **Stacked on #33451 (not merged when this PR opened).** This branch starts from that PR's head `3c1cdfab46`, so the first commits in the list are #33451's (the `SEARCH_COMPANION_FIELD` move into `@objectstack/spec/data` and the `validate_expression` fix). This PR's own change is the single commit `59ae25a92d`. Once #33451 lands, `origin/main` gets merged in and the diff becomes this commit alone.

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:MCP `describe_object` 在两个传输(HTTP 桥 `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`、stdio 桥与 `objectstack://objects/{name}` 资源 `packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts`)都不再列出隐藏的 `__search` 搜索伴随列。
- **为什么改**:开启拼音搜索时注册表给对象加了 `__search` 列,但任何调用方都不能读、写或点名它;`describe_object` 却把它当字段提供给 agent,与其它入口(记录读取、`$searchFields`、`validate_expression`)全都拒收相矛盾。
- **风险与回滚**:低。只在两处 `describeServedObject` 加一个按名过滤,常量来自 `@objectstack/spec/data`,无新依赖、不加载引擎;回滚即还原该提交。
- **先看**:`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`(HTTP 孪生的过滤行)、`packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts`(stdio 孪生的过滤行)、`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-object-schema-mask.test.ts`(真实引擎上的钉子)。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run src/domains/mcp-object-schema-mask.test.ts -t 'hidden search companion'`,预期 2 passed。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地(需先等 #33451 合并)。

## What changes

- `describeServedObject` in `packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts` (the stdio bridge's `describe_object` and the `objectstack://objects/{name}` resource) and its HTTP twin in `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` now skip the field named `SEARCH_COMPANION_FIELD`.
- Both import the constant from `@objectstack/spec/data`, the import #33451 uses in `mcp-http-tools.ts`. Neither file gains an engine import.
- No shared helper. The twins live in two packages and neither depends on the other, so the only shared home would be `@objectstack/spec`, which is outside this card's file surface. Each twin skips the field by the one protocol constant, so no second list exists.
- Every other served field is listed as before, including the injected system columns (`organization_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`).
- Changeset: `patch` for `@objectstack/mcp` and `@objectstack/runtime`.

## Tests

Two pins, each added as a top-level `describe` in the transport's existing describe_object harness:

- **HTTP**, `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp-object-schema-mask.test.ts`. Uses a real `ObjectQL` over a real `SqlDriver`, with `OS_SEARCH_PINYIN_ENABLED=true` (the switch the registry reads when it is built) and the protocol over that engine, driven through the real `/mcp` dispatcher entry.
  - Precondition: the registry's schema and `servedObjectDefinitionOf` both carry `__search`.
  - Assertion: the `describeObject` answer has no `__search` anywhere in its text, and still lists `name`, `email`, `created_at`, `updated_at` and `organization_id`.
- **stdio**, `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.object-schema-mask.test.ts`. The served object is built with the producer's own `provisionSearchCompanion(applyInjectedSystemColumns(...))`, not a transcription of its output.
  - Assertions: the same checks over the `describe_object` tool, called through a real MCP client, and over the `objectstack://objects/{name}` resource.

Measured before the fix (premise re-check): the HTTP pin failed with `expected [ 'organization_id', …(10) ] to not include '__search'`, and both stdio cases failed the same way.

<details><summary>Ablation (fix committed first, mutation through scripts/ablation-replace.mjs)</summary>

The first attempt passed an empty `--replacement`, which the tool refused because a zero-length replacement cannot be counted. No test ran on that attempt and its reading is void. It was re-run with `--delete`:

```
mcp-server-runtime.ts: anchor ".filter(([key]) => key !== SEARCH_COMPANION_FIELD)" x1 -> x0, blob f73e1a4c0998 -> d8011faa0adc
  × describe_object over stdio
  × the objectstack://objects/{name} resource
  restored: blob == HEAD (f73e1a4c0998), git diff HEAD empty
runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts: anchor ".filter(([k]) => k !== SEARCH_COMPANION_FIELD)" x1 -> x0, blob 8b51baf85364 -> e63a08356c4a
  × the answer has no companion, and keeps the declared fields and the platform's other system columns
  restored: blob == HEAD (8b51baf85364), git diff HEAD empty
```

Both suites import the edited module from source (relative imports), so no `dist/` sits between the mutation and the test.
</details>

<details><summary>Runs at 59ae25a92d</summary>

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: Test Files 64 passed (64), Tests 1180 passed (1180)
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 --project local src/domains`: Test Files 215 passed (215), Tests 5029 passed (5029)
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp run typecheck`: exit 0. `check:test-typecheck` OK.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime run typecheck`: exit 0. The first run went red on two untouched test files (`Cannot find module '@objectstack/driver-turso'`) because that package was not yet built in this fresh worktree. After building it: `check:test-typecheck: OK`.
- `eslint --no-inline-config` on the four touched source and test files: exit 0.
</details>

## Acceptance notes

- After this lands, the explicit companion skip in `validate_expression` (`mcp-http-tools.ts`, from #33451) is redundant whenever the bridge's `describeObject` is one of the two twins. It is left in place as that tool's own statement of its scope.
- `servedObjectDefinitionOf` still returns the served definition whole, companion included. That is the definition `validate_expression` hands the publish gate's passes, and this card does not change it.

## Verification

Gate families derived by `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` at 59ae25a92d, then reconciled with `--ran`. The change set includes #33451's commits because the branch is stacked on it. The per-family verdicts are in the os-dev report comment on #33454.
